inline.s: [Someone says: For one who has not yet reached the true mind, because he is deluded about the true mind, he creates causes of good and evil. Because he creates good causes, he is born in the good realms; because he creates evil causes, he enters the evil realms, and is born in accord with his karma; of this principle there is no doubt. But for one who has reached the true mind, false feelings utterly exhausted, and having realized and verified the true mind, there are no causes of good or evil; after this one spirit departs, what does it rely upon? It is answered: Do not suppose that one who has something to rely upon is superior to one who has nothing to rely upon! And do not liken the one who has nothing to rely upon to a wanderer adrift in the human world, or to a masterless orphan ghost of the ghost realm, and so raise this question only to seek to have something to rely upon.]

The questioner says: For one who has not yet reached the true mind, because he is deluded about the true mind, he creates causes of good and evil. Because he creates good causes, he is born in the good realms; because he creates evil causes, he enters the evil realms; and they are all born in accord with the karma they have created. I have no doubt about this principle. But for one who has reached the true mind, false feelings utterly exhausted, and having realized and verified the true mind, there are no causes of good or evil; then, after this body departs, what does this spirit rely upon? The answer says: Do not suppose that one who has something to rely upon is superior to one who has nothing to rely upon! And do not liken the one without reliance to a wanderer adrift in the human world, or to a masterless orphan ghost of the ghost realm, and therefore raise this question only to seek to have something to rely upon.
[After this body] After death.
[Someone says: So be it. It is answered: For one who has reached the nature, it is not so. Because all living beings are deluded about the awakened nature, they forget
(are false,)

feelings, love, and thoughts, and gather karma as their cause, and are born in the six realms, receiving the retribution of good and evil. If heavenly karma is the cause, one obtains only the heavenly fruit; apart from the place of his fitting birth, in all the rest he receives no enjoyment, and so it is in every realm. Since he follows his karma, the place of his fitting birth is happiness and the place of his non-birth is not happiness; he takes the place of his fitting birth as his own reliance and the place of his non-birth as the reliance of others. Therefore, if there are false feelings, there are false causes; if there are false causes, there are false fruits; if there are false fruits, there is reliance; if there is reliance, there is the distinction of this and that; if there is this and that, then there is that which is acceptable and that which is not.]

The questioner says: So it is. The answerer says: For one who has penetrated the awakened nature, it is not so. Because all living beings are deluded about the awakened nature, false feelings, love, and thoughts create all kinds of karma and become the cause of the turning wheel, and so they are born in the six realms, receiving the retribution of good and evil. If heavenly karma is the cause, one obtains only the heavenly fruit; apart from the place of his fitting birth, in the rest he obtains no enjoyment of the heavenly fruit; and so it is in all the other realms. Since they are born following their karma, they take the place of fitting birth as happiness and the place of non-birth as not happiness. Therefore they take the place of fitting birth as their own reliance and the place of non-birth as the reliance of others. So, if there are false feelings, there are false causes; if there are false causes, there are false fruits; if there are false fruits, there is reliance; if there is reliance, there is the division of this and that; if there is this and that, then there are places where one can be born and places where one cannot be born.
[The place of fitting birth] The place where one should be born, one of the six realms. [The place of non-birth] The place where one is not born, the remaining realms of the six.

[Now, having reached the true mind, one accords with the awakened nature that is without arising and ceasing, and rouses the wondrous functioning that is without arising and ceasing. The wondrous substance is true and eternal, originally without arising or ceasing; the wondrous functioning follows conditions and so seems to have arising and ceasing. Yet since the functioning arises from the substance, and the functioning is the substance, how could there be any arising or ceasing? The one who has reached it realizes the true substance; what do arising and ceasing have to do with him? It is like water, whose substance is wetness and whose function is the waves. Because wetness is originally without arising or ceasing, how could the wetness within the waves have arising or ceasing? And because the waves do not exist apart from wetness, the waves likewise have no arising or ceasing. Therefore the ancients said: 'The whole earth is the single true eye of the sramana; the whole earth is a monastery.' All of it is the place where one who understands the principle settles his body and establishes his life.]

Now, having penetrated the true mind, one accords with the awakened nature that is without arising and ceasing, and rouses the wondrous functioning that is without arising and ceasing. The wondrous substance of the true mind is true and eternal, originally without arising or ceasing; while the wondrous functioning follows conditions and seems to have arising and ceasing. Yet, since the functioning arises from the substance, and the functioning is the substance, since the substance is without arising or ceasing, how could the functioning have arising or ceasing? Therefore one who has penetrated the true mind realizes the true substance; what has the illusion of arising and ceasing to do with him? For example, water takes wetness as its substance and the waves as its functioning. Because wetness is originally without arising or ceasing, how could the wetness within the waves have arising or ceasing? Yet, because the waves do not exist apart from wetness, therefore the waves too are without arising or ceasing. (This is a simile: the rising of a wave is birth and the stilling of the wave is death; whether the wave rises or stills, the essence of wetness is always there.) Therefore the ancients said: 'The whole earth is the true mind of this monk; the whole earth is the monastery where this monk dwells.' Therefore every place is the place where one who understands the principle settles his body and establishes his life.

[Sramana] Rendered in Chinese as 'diligent stilling,' that is, diligent in cultivating the Buddha Way and stilling the various afflictions; a general term for one who has left home to practice the Way. [The right eye] That is, the true mind; see 'Chapter Two: The Different Names of the True Mind.' [Gharama] An abbreviation of samgharama, rendered in Chinese as 'garden of the assembly,' that is, the grounds where the community of monks dwells, and a general term for a monastery.

[Having reached the true mind, the four kinds of birth and the six realms all vanish in an instant; mountains, rivers, and the whole earth are all the true mind, and one cannot apart from this true mind have another place of reliance. Since there are no false causes in the three realms, there must indeed be no false fruits in the six destinies. Since there are no false fruits, what reliance can be spoken of? There must be no this and that. Since there is no this and that, then what is acceptable and what is not? In the ten directions and all the world there is only the one true mind, enjoyed with the whole body, with no other reliance; and in the gate of manifestation, one may be reborn at will, without obstruction.]

Since one has penetrated the true mind, the four kinds of birth and the six realms vanish at once, and mountains, rivers, and the whole earth are all the true mind of this person; one cannot apart from this true mind have another place of reliance. Since there are no false causes of the three realms, there must indeed be no false fruits of the six realms. Since there are no false fruits of the six realms, what reliance is there to speak of? There must be no distinction of this place and that place. Since there is no distinction of this and that, then wherever one is it is all the same, so what is acceptable and what is not? Throughout the ten directions and all worlds there is only the one true mind, enjoyed fully with the whole body, without any other reliance; and in the gate of manifestation, one may be reborn at will, without obstruction.

[The four kinds of birth] Viviparous birth, oviparous birth, moisture-born birth, and miraculously-born birth. Viviparous birth is life that takes shape within the mother's womb before being born, as with humans; oviparous birth is life that takes shape within an eggshell before being born, as with birds; moisture-born birth is life that takes shape relying on moisture, as with worms; miraculously-born birth is life that has no dependence but, by the power of karma alone, suddenly comes into being, as with the devas and hell-beings and the humans of the beginning of a kalpa. [The six realms] The devas, humans, asuras, animals, hungry ghosts, and hell-beings. Because these six are the places where all living beings go in accord with their karma, they are also called the 'six destinies.' [The three realms] The realm of desire, the realm of form, and the formless realm. The realm of desire is the world where beings with the two desires of sex and food dwell, from the six heavens of desire above, through the four great continents where humans and animals dwell in the middle, down to the unintermitted hell below; the realm of form is the world where beings without the two desires of sex and food but still having material form dwell, all belonging to the four dhyanas and eighteen heavens; the formless realm is the world where beings without form or matter but dwelling the mind and consciousness in deep meditative concentration dwell, all belonging to the four heavens of the formless. These three realms are all the spheres where ordinary beings pass back and forth through birth and death, and therefore the goal of the Buddhist practitioner is to leap beyond the three realms.

[Therefore the Transmission of the Lamp says: 'Minister Wen Cao asked Guifeng: When one who understands the principle reaches the end of his allotted life, where does he rely? Guifeng said: All living beings without exception possess the numinous, bright awakened nature, no different from the Buddha. If one can awaken to this nature, it is the dharmakaya, originally without arising; how could there be any reliance? It is numinous and bright, not dim, ever clear and knowing, come from nowhere, gone to nowhere. Only take emptiness and stillness as your own substance, do not take the physical body as yourself; only take numinous knowing as your own mind, do not take false thoughts as yourself.
If false thoughts arise, do not follow any of them; then at the end of life, karma will naturally be unable to tether you.
Though there be an intermediate state, one may go freely, and in the heavens or among humans take up one's abode at will; this is where the aforementioned true mind goes after the body.'

Therefore the Transmission of the Lamp says: 'Minister Wen Cao asked Master Guifeng: When one who understands the principle reaches the end of his allotted life, where does he go to find reliance? Guifeng said: All living beings without exception possess the numinous, bright awakened nature (the true mind), no different from the Buddha. If one can awaken to this awakened nature, it is the dharmakaya, originally without arising; how could there be any reliance? The dharmakaya is numinous and bright, not dim, ever clear and knowing, come from nowhere, gone to nowhere. If one takes only the empty and still dharmakaya as one's own body, and does not falsely grasp the physical body as oneself; if one takes only numinous knowing as one's own mind, and does not falsely grasp false thoughts as one's own mind; and if false thoughts arise and one follows none of them, then at the end of life karma naturally cannot tether him. Though there be an intermediate body, one may go freely, and in the heavens or among humans take up one's abode at will.'

[Numinous knowing] It is the true knowing of no-thought, that is, the knowing of the true mind spoken of in the previous chapter. Numinous knowing is knowing without grasping at marks; to distinguish it from the mark-grasping knowing of seeing, hearing, perception, and awareness, it is called numinous knowing. The Record of the Mirror of the Teaching says: 'Prajna's non-knowing is the absence of mark-grasping knowing.' The Surangama Sutra says: 'To establish a view within views is the root of ignorance; when views are free of seeing, this is nirvana, the pure and true, without outflows.' Great Master Hanshan, in his Reading Notes on the Lankavatara, says: 'When the mind is still and knowing, both true and false are left behind; this is called the saintly wisdom of self-realization.' Great Master Yongjia, in the Yongjia Collection of the Chan School

in the fourth of the Verses on Shamatha, says: 'After forgetting conditions, it is still and still; the nature of numinous knowing is distinct and distinct.' Seng Zhao, in his Treatise on the Non-Knowing of Prajna, says: 'Because the sage's mind is without knowing, therefore it knows everything. The knowing of not-knowing is called all-knowing. Therefore the sutra says: "The sage's mind knows nothing and yet knows everything." This is trustworthy indeed!' [The intermediate state] The intermediate body, also called the intermediate existence; that is, before a person is reborn after death there is a miraculously born body formed of subtle matter that maintains life, and this miraculously born body is precisely the intermediate body. In the first forty-nine days this intermediate body undergoes a birth-and-death every seven days, passing through seven rounds of birth and death, and then, awaiting the disposal of its karmic conditions, goes to take rebirth.
The Essentials of the Mind-Dharma Transmission says:

"When a person is approaching the end of life, only contemplate that the five aggregates are all empty, the four elements are without self, and the true mind is without marks, neither going nor coming. At birth the nature
(the awakened nature)
does not come, and at death the nature does not go; serene and perfectly still, mind and realm are one. If one can thus comprehend it in a single stroke, and be unbound by the three times
(past, present, and future)
, then one is a person beyond the world."
